newsitem.title: USA: FDA warns Medtronic on pump manufacturing.
newsitem.headline: FDA warns Medtronic on pump manufacturing.

text.p: Medtronic Inc said it received a warning letter from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration concerning some testing equipment used in the manufacture of its Bio-Pump centrifugal blood pump.
The company said it has taken steps to address the FDA's concerns. "We have responded and taken the corrective actions we said we would take," said company spokesman Dick Reid.
The agency inspected Medtronic on August 16 and issued the warning letter under its "best manufacturing practices" rules on August 30, Reid said.
"It relates to some concerns they had about some testing equipment used in the manufacture of that pump," he said.
The Bio-Pump is sold by Medtronic for use during heart surgery, when it acts as a substitute heart by pumping blood through a heart-lung bypass circuit.
"It's not the product. It's the manufacturing process," Reid said, adding that the testing equipment cited by the FDA as inadequate has been recalibrated.
"We expect to allay their concerns," he said.
